hook: SCP-1193 starts as a measurement problem and turns into a phone call. Read the numbers in the description with care, because the article quietly expects you to do the scaling in your head. The transcripts at the end are where the tone shifts from dry to oddly funny and uncomfortable.
whyItMatters: The page carries the reviewers-spotlight tag, and it shows how much a compact file can do with one description and two short transcripts. It never draws the whole creature; you assemble the picture yourself from depths, elbow counts and offhand complaints. That reliance on inference over reveal is the technique worth taking away from it.
thingsToNotice: Put the numbers together and the picture is enormous: an arm with an elbow every four kilometres, reaching past 71 km into the mantle at over 674 degrees, belongs to someone who calls it simply his bottom arm. The list of things the caller mentions doubles as a second description in everyday language, from a jelly jar to a gopher hole, sketching a giant body from the inside. Dr. Iqbal agreeing that he is from the hospital is a small human moment that also shows how the Foundation gets information out of the caller. The second call, exactly a year later, has David wedged in a stove after reaching for cakes, groaning about his back, then saying he is calling his cousin and apologising that it isn't his fault. Read against the seismic monitors and Protocol 473a, which severs the arm below the fifth elbow, that apology suggests whatever is coming to pick him up is something the Foundation should dread.
